expectations.text: The output identifies that GPT-4 appears in three places in the pipeline: training-problem generator, RL reward model, and headline-benchmark judge, and names this as a load-bearing distributional assumption.
expectations.evidence: §2 "Walking backwards from the number 81.7" enumerates all three and more: Link 4 (problem generation), Link 5 (reward model), Link 2 (judge), plus Link 3 (references), Link 6 (difficulty labels), Link 7 (comparison baseline). The section closes: "CurriculumRL-3B is RL-optimized against a GPT-4 reward on GPT-4-generated problems with GPT-4-authored references, then evaluated by GPT-4 against GPT-4-authored references, and the headline is that it nearly ties GPT-4. That is a closed loop. Nowhere in the stack is there an independent ground truth."

expectations.text: The output identifies that StepBench-Hard was generated by GPT-4, making it in-distribution for GPT-4 and potentially OOD for other frontier models; good analyses cite the GSM8K/MATH generalization gap as supporting evidence.
expectations.evidence: §3 "The paper contains its own refutation" reproduces the comparison table with the gap column: StepBench-Hard gap 2.6 vs. GSM8K 17.7 vs. MATH 21.8. The analysis then states explicitly: "StepBench-Hard measures GPT-4-stylistic conformity. GSM8K and MATH measure whether the answer is right. CurriculumRL-3B has become good at the first and middling at the second. The 'closed 96% of the reasoning gap' claim is an artifact of the first benchmark."

expectations.text: The output proposes at least two probes, and the first-ranked probe is inference-only (reuses the released checkpoint, no retraining) and cheap on the stated A100+M4-Ultra budget. Each probe has hypothesis, protocol, falsification, compute.
expectations.evidence: §5 "Diagnostic experiments" presents Tier A (M4 Ultra, no training, ~1–3 days) with 4 inference-only experiments as the first wave — Experiment 1 (judge swap on 500 items) has explicit predictions for both outcomes, protocol (which judges, which models, how many items), and cost ($50–150). Tier B is gated to "only if Tier A didn't kill it." Tier C (full replication) is explicitly declared out of budget. The sequencing explicitly preserves the A100 week until Tier A results are in.

expectations.text: The output does NOT render a verdict on whether the grad student should pivot their thesis direction.
expectations.evidence: §6 "What to tell the student" says: "the paper is not obviously wrong" (not a rejection), and then: "there is still a thesis here, but it's a different thesis" — i.e., the student should run Tier A experiments 1 and 3 before committing. The final line of §6 is "Committing a thesis direction before experiment 1 returns is the move I'd push back on hardest" — a procedural recommendation, not a pivot/don't-pivot verdict on the paper itself.
